title: Stabilize a wobbling cutting board while keeping a mug upright
instruction: Fit the spare black pad under the short foot so the cutting board sits level. Keep the mug on the board within 4.5 cm of its starting spot on the board and within 25 degrees of upright. Let go when finished.
context: A cutting board missing one rubber foot rocks under load. With a mug resting above the short foot, the board must be supported while seating a pad beneath it. The task measures whether the robot can restore stable support while keeping the loose load in place.
setup: Positions are in cm on the station tabletop from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left, heights above tabletop z 0. Cutting board: solid oiled walnut butcher-block slab with a pale maple inlay strip, 18.0 cm deep (x) by 24.0 cm wide (y) by 2.8 cm thick, 0.95 kg including hardware, centered at (28.0, 0.0) cm. Four feet sit 1.6 cm inset from the outer edges at offsets (+-7.4, +-10.4) cm from board center: three intact black SBR rubber bumper feet (32 mm diameter, 20 mm tall with 4 mm steel washers) and one bare brushed-brass stud with a red mounting collar (21.8 mm diameter, 12 mm tall — 8 mm shorter than the rubber feet). The bare foot is at the front-left corner (20.6, +10.4) cm. Open mug: white glazed stoneware cylinder, 7.0 cm diameter by 9.5 cm tall, 0.42 kg including water filled to a blue level mark 2 cm below its rim, standing on top of the board above the missing-foot quadrant at (-3.6, +5.6) cm relative to board center so gravity presses the bare brass stud flush onto the tabletop (0 mm air gap at rest, 3.8 deg tilt toward that corner). Spare rubber pad: matte black EPDM square-corner pad, 4.4 cm deep (x) by 3.6 cm wide (y) by 8 mm thick, 25 g, with a centered 14 x 14 mm steel washer plate on top, lying flat on the table at (12.5, 0.0) cm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged throughout the trial for hazards, and at the end for outcome (SCORE_OVER = end). Latched hazards (score 0.0 for the entire trial if held for 2 consecutive control steps / 0.1 s): the open mug tilts more than 25 deg from vertical, drops below the board top, or leaves its spot on the board (> 4.5 cm displacement in board coordinates); or the cutting board tilts more than 18 deg, shifts more than 6.0 cm horizontally from start, or drops below the tabletop. Otherwise: 1.0 (success, held for 1.0 s / 20 steps) when the spare pad lies flat on the table (<= 10 deg tilt, underside within 4 mm of tabletop) centered within 1.2 cm of the bare brass foot center, the bare stud bottom rests at 5 to 11 mm above tabletop (within 3 mm of the top face of the 8 mm pad), the cutting board lies flat within 0.8 deg of level, the mug stands upright within 5 deg on its board spot, all three objects are still (< 5 mm/s and < 5 deg/s), and no gripper palm or finger touches any object (<= 2 mm contact margin). 0.75 when the pad is seated within 1.2 cm at 5 to 11 mm foot height and within 3 mm of the top face, with the board flat within 1.2 deg and mug within 5 deg, while still touched or settling. 0.50 when the spare pad lies flat within 2.5 cm of the bare foot, or when the bare foot bottom is lifted at least 6 mm clear above the tabletop while the pad is within 6.0 cm. 0.25 when the spare pad has moved at least 2.5 cm toward the bare corner (or within 9.0 cm of it). 0.0 otherwise, including doing nothing. Real trial verification: read board flatness with a spirit level or protractor (<= 0.8 deg), verify pad alignment against a 1.2 cm circle marked under the bare foot, and confirm visual stillness and release.
reset_notes: Gently lift the front corner to slide out the spare pad, return the spare pad flat to (12.5, 0.0) cm, set the cutting board back on its outline so the bare corner rests on the tabletop, and verify mug water fill is 2 cm below the rim (wiping dry first if any spilled).
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX at 240 Hz with 20 Hz robot control. Compound props model the board, feet and weighted mug. Ceramic-on-wood friction is 0.45. The mug render shows a recessed water surface. The simulator uses a rigid collision envelope and fill mass. The scoring measures mug pose. Liquid motion is outside the simulation.
scores: Dream-1 (FL): 0.00 in 2,400 steps. Scripted two-arm demo (FL): 1.00 in 417 steps.
